title: Existence of a doubling constant for an ergodic countable abelian action is equivalent to an infinite Kronecker factor
difficulty_reason: H2: a compact factor attached to one fixed pair does not provide the global small-set doubling characterization. The author turns a whole sequence of shrinking positive-measure sets with one uniform doubling constant into a single infinite compact factor by closing the diagonal image in a countable product, retaining the small Haar-measure witnesses. For the converse the proof separates an infinite totally disconnected quotient, which supplies decreasing open-subgroup witnesses, from a finite-index connected component, where a surjective character and shrinking arcs supply the two-doubling witnesses. This all-scales factor construction and the two topological realizations are the claim-specific nonroutine core; the old measurable correspondence is provided but is not counted again.

compared.relation: Exact Theorem1.8 for one critical pair in a totally ergodic action gives a circleinterval factor with endpointcoset exceptions; no all-scales characterization of the action.
Exact Theorem1.5 controls one strict-subcritical pair by a finite quotient; new primary instead characterizes uniform C-doubling at arbitrarily small scales by an infinite compact factor.
Actual Theorem1.2 large-radius small doubling of symmetric open sets yields bounded tripling/approximate groups in locally compact groups, not a measure-preserving action or Kronecker factor.
Actual Theorem4.1 lifts an automorphism of a fixed-point C-star algebra iff twisted factor systems are conjugate; not a probability-action small-set inverse theorem.
Actual Theorem4.1 constructs conformally perturbed spectral triples from compact Lie C-star ergodic actions; not infinite Kronecker factors or transfer-density doubling.
